messages:
maria: FYI we just got an escalation from support about a customer reporting p95/p99 regressions since ~03:40 UTC. They see long tail on short prompts, many are ~10 tokens.
jon: link to ticket?
maria: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-8445 — customer id redwood-cust-42. Says median fine, but p99 jumped from 220ms -> 1.1s.
li: saw similar in global dashboards, spike aligns with a config rollout at 03:35 where we adjusted continuous batching defaults for prod (increased max_batch_wait from 5ms -> 12ms to improve throughput).
andrew: that change was to save cost on hosted tier A. didn't expect regressions on tiny requests.
maria: support noted some API 429s interleaved and a few 500s (backend kv cache timeouts) but primary complaint is latency tail.
jon: initial hypothesis: increasing wait improves throughput for medium prompts but hurts tiny prompt tail because hold-window allows many tiny requests to wait and then microburst scheduling causes a serialization/queueing effect on worker loop.
li: digging traces — for redwood-cust-42 we have many requests hitting the continuous-batcher with hold_window ~= 12ms, but due to request arrival jitter some requests wait almost full window and then see an extra ~800ms in pooling + kernel warmup when batched with larger sequence lengths.
maria: repro steps from support (they ran a simple curl loop):
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}' &
sleep 0.003
done
```
Responses: most <300ms, intermittent ~1.1s.
jon: I can repro locally with a small harness that simulates poisson arrivals. Will attach logs.
jon: logs show continuous-batcher wait path: request enters, scheduled to batch, then deferred to bg worker that has a backlog because a couple of medium-length requests (seq=1024) triggered longer kernel prep -> queueing.
li: so interaction between hold_window and heterogeneous seq lengths. Also noticed a small bug where tiny_request_bypass was disabled for that customer tier after the rollout (config merge missed a flag).
andrew: oof. so two issues: (1) larger hold_window increase; (2) bypass flag disabled -> tiny requests forced into common batching path.
support-lead: customer wants mitigation ASAP, they're hitting user-facing timeouts.
jon: short-term mitigation options:
- revert hold_window change (global rollback)
- re-enable tiny_request_bypass for tier A (targeted config change)
- add a runtime policy to bypass batching for requests with tokens <= 16
- enable canary routing to dedicated nodes for that customer
maria: what about rolling back vs targeted patch?
li: targeted is faster and lowest blast radius. I can flip tiny_request_bypass back for tier A in the config service (no infra deploy).
jon: also lower hold_window to 6ms as a compromise.
andrew: I'll prepare both changes: patch bypass flag and reduce hold_window to 6ms. Apply to prod with 5% canary then 100% if green.
deploy-bot: Deployment started by andrew: config-service update (tiny_request_bypass=tierA:true, continuous_batching.max_hold_ms=6) — canary 5%
maria: monitoring: watching p95/p99 and customer ticket. set alert for p99 > 600ms.
li: after canary stats: p99 for the affected flow dropped from ~1.1s -> 420ms, p95 stable ~260ms. No increase in 429s observed.
andrew: promoting to 100% now.
deploy-bot: Deployment complete: config-service update promoted to 100% at 03:56 UTC.
support-lead: told customer we deployed a fix and asked them to verify. Customer confirmed latency improved, still a few single-digit occurrences but acceptable.
jon: root cause writeup draft: interaction between increased hold_window and disabled tiny_request_bypass combined with heterogeneous sequence lengths leads to batching-induced tail spikes. Also found edge case where bypass flag config path was skipped during merge.
li: action items:
- revert global default change on hold_window unless we have per-workload tuning (PR already rolled back to 6ms)
- add automated test in CI simulating mixed sequence workloads to detect tail regressions
- add a canary rule that prevents hold_window increases >8ms without perf signoff
- fix config merge tool to ensure tiny_request_bypass flags are preserved (ticket INFR-8448)
- run a billing/impact analysis for throughput changes before next rollout
maria: I've updated the Jira with timeline and customer notes.
andrew: I'll open a small PR for the config merge fix and link it to INFR-8448.
jon: adding a short runbook snippet in ops-runbooks: how to triage batching tail spikes (check bypass flag, hold_window, trace examples, quick mitigations).
maria: thanks all, closing loop with customer. We'll keep monitoring 24h. :thumbsup:
